Read and Validate Multi-Band Stack Raster

Source: R/read_stack.R
d4h_read_stack.Rd

Loads a multi-band raster stack from a file or SpatRaster, verifies that required spectral or terrain bands are present, and throws an informative error if any required band is missing.

Usage

d4h_read_stack(file_path, required_bands = NULL, band_names = NULL)

d4h_load_stack(file_path, required_bands = NULL, band_names = NULL)

Arguments

file_path

Character path or SpatRaster. File path to a multi-band GeoTIFF/raster file, or an existing SpatRaster object.

required_bands

Character vector (optional). Names of bands that must be present in the stack (e.g. c("NIR", "Red")). Matching is case-insensitive.

band_names

Character vector (optional). Layer names to assign or override on the raster stack. Must match the number of layers if provided.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster object with validated layers and band names.

Details

In drone remote sensing pipelines, multi-band orthomosaics often combine optical (Red, Green, Blue), Red Edge, Near-Infrared (NIR), and digital elevation (DEM/DSM) channels into a single stacked GeoTIFF. d4h_read_stack reads the multi-layer raster, assigns or verifies layer names, and strictly validates that all bands required for downstream metric calculations (such as NDVI or NDWI) exist in the stack. If a required band is absent, execution halts immediately with an informative error listing the missing band(s) and currently available layers.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (interactive()) {
  library(drones4health)

  # Define path to multi-band drone raster stack
  stack_file <- system.file("extdata", "ortho_multiband.tif", package = "drones4health")

  # Read stack and assert presence of NIR and Red bands
  r_stack <- d4h_read_stack(
    file_path      = stack_file,
    required_bands = c("NIR", "Red")
  )
  print(r_stack)
}
# }
